assumptions.statement: All sample spaces are standard Borel and all declared kernels and transport maps are measurable.
Private priors, likelihood kernels, transported sources, and source rows are normalized.
History H_n is fixed during the n+1 recognition update, so the generative joint is independent of Q^{n+1}.
The recognition laws satisfy the needed absolute-continuity and logarithmic-finiteness conditions, or the displayed chain rules are interpreted as valid extended-real identities.
Private and relational replicas represent distinct informational roles of the same displayed belief and model state.
For the gauge claim, the fiber coordinate changes are bimeasurable bijections and the likelihood density is transformed covariantly.

claims.statement: For every fixed finite agent-site index set and every admissible standard-Borel two-channel datum with normalized private priors, normalized likelihood kernels, normalized positive source rows, lagged transported source laws, and the stated absolute-continuity and finiteness conditions, prove that the tied-replica construction defines a normalized generative joint independent of the current recognition law and that its unit-temperature negative ELBO equals the finite lagged two-channel PIFB2 scalar plus the state-model mutual-information correction; prove exact equality with that PIFB2 scalar under state-model mean field and prove invariance under the declared simultaneous fiber-coordinate pushforwards.
claims.quantifiers: For every nonempty finite agent-site set A, every finite source set in each active relational channel, and every collection of standard-Borel probability data satisfying the declared normalization, measurability, absolute-continuity, and finiteness hypotheses.
claims.falsifier: An admissible normalized datum violates normalization, the ELBO identity, the mean-field specialization, or simultaneous-pushforward invariance.

claims.statement: The conditional tied-replica generative joint and the restricted recognition law are normalized for every admitted finite datum.
claims.quantifiers: For every nonempty finite agent-site set A, every finite source set in each active relational channel, and every collection of standard-Borel probability data satisfying the declared normalization, measurability, absolute-continuity, and finiteness hypotheses.
claims.falsifier: An admitted factor or finite product fails to integrate to one.

claims.statement: The negative ELBO equals the two marginal self KLs, the observation term, two categorical row KLs, two weighted transported peer KL sectors, and the private state-model mutual information.
claims.quantifiers: For every nonempty finite agent-site set A, every finite source set in each active relational channel, and every collection of standard-Borel probability data satisfying the declared normalization, measurability, absolute-continuity, and finiteness hypotheses.
claims.falsifier: A valid Radon-Nikodym example violates one of the two KL chain-rule expansions.

claims.statement: Under zeta_a=q_a tensor s_a, the mutual-information correction vanishes and the exact ELBO equals the lagged unit-temperature, unit-private-coefficient finite PIFB2 scalar.
claims.quantifiers: For every nonempty finite agent-site set A, every finite source set in each active relational channel, and every collection of standard-Borel probability data satisfying the declared normalization, measurability, absolute-continuity, and finiteness hypotheses.
claims.falsifier: A product private recognition law has nonzero mutual information or a retained unit PIFB2 term is absent from the exact expansion.

claims.statement: The exact finite scalar is invariant under the declared simultaneous bimeasurable fiber-coordinate pushforwards and covariant likelihood transformation.
claims.quantifiers: For every nonempty finite agent-site set A, every finite source set in each active relational channel, and every collection of standard-Borel probability data satisfying the declared normalization, measurability, absolute-continuity, and finiteness hypotheses.
claims.falsifier: A declared bijective pushforward changes any KL or likelihood contribution.

claims.statement: Measurable one-step kernels of the stated form assemble into a normalized finite-horizon adaptive process conditional on stored law-valued histories.
claims.quantifiers: For every nonempty finite agent-site set A, every finite source set in each active relational channel, and every collection of standard-Borel probability data satisfying the declared normalization, measurability, absolute-continuity, and finiteness hypotheses.
claims.falsifier: An admitted finite iterated kernel fails normalization or measurability.

claims.statement: The theorem derives the same-time reciprocal live-peer PIFB2 scalar from one fixed normalized joint on shared contemporaneous agent variables.
claims.quantifiers: For every nonempty finite agent-site set A, every finite source set in each active relational channel, and every collection of standard-Borel probability data satisfying the declared normalization, measurability, absolute-continuity, and finiteness hypotheses.
claims.falsifier: A fixed normalized shared-variable construction proves it; contemporaneous recognition dependence or a normalization cycle defeats the proposed construction.
